page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated graphics processing units, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the ecs.sn2.large in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute instances. In stress-ng testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% tier, with scores of 1105.28 and 2929.74 respectively. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large-block read-only operations registering at 21.24 GB/sec and write operations at 18.69 GB/sec. Similarly, Geekbench and Passmark testing indicate weak to poor execution speeds across single-core and multi-core workloads, including software compilation, text processing, and database operations.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the ecs.sn2.large represents a legacy tier of compute resources. Its qualitative cost efficiency is characterized by its dedicated CPU allocation, which avoids resource contention but delivers lower absolute performance per core compared to newer architectures. This instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads that require dedicated CPU cores but do not demand high-throughput processing, such as low-traffic web serving, basic Redis caching, or minor background utility tasks.
